newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH FINMIN SEE SMALL FLOOD IMPACT ON ECONOMY.
newsitem.headline: POLISH FINMIN SEE SMALL FLOOD IMPACT ON ECONOMY.

text.p: Polish Finance Minister Marek Belka said on Wednesday that July's heavy flooding was unlikely to significantly slow down the country's economic growth and create strong inflationary pressure.
"The Polish economy is like a rushing locomotive, which the flood will not be able to stop," Belka told a news conference.
He said he based his optimism on excellent revenues in July from the corporate tax, which would have been much worse had the flood caused significant damages in the economy.

"There is a possiblity that in the first two months we will see a slow down because growth of industrial production will be somewhat smaller. But in a long-term perspective I foresee no statistically significant GDP slow down," he said.
The central bank's president Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz has said the flood was likely to cut GDP growth by up to one point. The government's official GDP growth forecast is 5.5 percent.
Belka said the flood's impact on inflation would be small. "If it has an effect on inflation it would not be big," he said.
He reiterated pledges to finance the reconstruction of areas hit by the flood in such a way so as to cause as little inflation as possible.
He said the finance ministry would limit the use of the inflation-fuelling 2.5-billion loan from the central bank for the relief operation.

"We know today that we are not going to take advantage of the whole of the credit," Belka said. He added that nothing has yet been spent from the one billion zlotys already drawn up up from the credit.
"The one billion has not yet been nibbed off and if there is no need to use it will not use it," he said.
He added that even if a part of the one-billion-zloty tranche was used, it would not send a strong inflationary impulse, because it would have to be repaid by the end of the year.
